channel.title: Edgeless Lab Blog
channel.description: Agent experiments, developer tools, and creative coding from a solo lab.

item.title: Generation Left the Screen
item.description: Two and a half years ago, AI video was the story. Looking back at five generative-AI videos, the most useful thing in the set is a free Minecraft mod from one independent researcher. Here's what that says about where generation went next.

item.title: Enterprise AI's Real Bottleneck Is Everything Around the Model
item.description: Six videos, one shared conclusion: the models work. What fails is the organization, the data policy and the infrastructure around them.

item.title: crt-shader: An Open-Source CRT Shader for WebGL 2
item.description: A self-contained WebGL 2 fragment shader that renders CRT monitor effects in-browser. No dependencies, no plugins, no post-processing stack.

item.title: Tick 151: The Heartbeat That Wasn't Real
item.description: A scheduled job wrote fake heartbeat statuses to the swarm's coordination file for four hours. The fix was rate-limited. Here is how we make sure it cannot happen again.

item.title: 9 OSS Alternatives Evaluated, 3 Adopted
item.description: We evaluated 9 open-source replacements for our SaaS stack. Three made the cut, and each one is better than what it replaced, not just cheaper.

item.title: edgeless.wei: On-Chain Identity, One Domain at a Time
item.description: We registered edgeless.wei as the canonical on-chain identity for the swarm. One domain, one identity, no namespace sprawl.

item.title: The Week "pip install" Became the Last Mile
item.description: Four videos, one devlog series, one packaging tool: Poetry is the bridge between 'it works on my machine' and 'pip install', and the diffbro series shows it's the last mile of AI tooling distribution.

item.title: The Week CLIs Became AI's Distribution Channel
item.description: Four videos, one series, one tool: diffbro is a pip-installable CLI that runs git diffs through ChatGPT for AI peer review — and it tells us something about where AI tooling is headed.

item.title: The Week Agentic Engineering's Hidden Crisis: Resource Collision
item.description: When N agents run in parallel they collide on ports, worktrees, databases, and token budgets — with no detection, isolation, or recovery. The binding constraint on parallel agent teams isn't model capability, it's resource allocation.

item.title: The Verification Chain Crisis: Why Multi-Agent Systems Fail Invisible
item.description: Six videos, one week, one recurring failure mode: the cheapest node in your orchestration graph rots the whole output. The specific mechanical fixes from chained verification stacks to deliberative panels.

item.title: The Week Agentic Engineering Became a Real Discipline
item.description: Nine YouTube videos, one week, zero hype. The shift from prompting to systems architecture is happening in plain sight — here's what it means for your agent stack.

item.title: The Week Multi-Agent Orchestration Stopped Being Optional
item.description: Seven YouTube videos, one week, one conclusion: one agent is not enough. The convergence on multi-agent orchestration as a design discipline, not a scaling afterthought.

item.title: The Gateway That Broke and the Expensive Models We Didn't Need
item.description: FreeLLMAPI had been quietly routing a small agent swarm across more than a dozen providers. Then the setup collapsed to four, its premium credential vanished, and activation started failing. Recovering it taught me that the real upgrade was not a pricier model. It was one source of truth and intentional routing.

item.title: Rescuing an AI Product From a Dying Platform in Four Weeks
item.description: A healthcare AI product was built on a no-code LLM platform that announced shutdown with a month of notice. How a solo rebuild on Azure hit the deadline with zero downtime, and what it says about platform risk in the LLM era.

item.title: Kimi K3: The "New Kimmy Moment" That Should Change How You Think About Your Stack
item.description: Kimi K3 offers frontier AI quality at a fraction of the cost – a new Kimmy moment that could reshape your stack.

item.title: 710 Tasks and the Bottleneck That Wasn't
item.description: My task board had 710 open items and I was sure the holdup was me — the human reviewer. Then I actually counted. My real decision queue was 69. Measure before you believe.

item.title: The Bot That Was Online But Couldn't Talk
item.description: A chat agent showed green, connected, running — and ignored every message. The culprit was a second adapter it didn't even need, crash-looping on a port collision.

item.title: The Monitor That Cried Wolf
item.description: My health monitor paged me about three dead services. All three were fine. The monitor was measuring the wrong thing and calling its own blind spot an outage. Verify the measurement before you chase the symptom.

item.title: Six Dispatchers Where One Is Law
item.description: My agent swarm had exactly one rule about who assigns work. The config said so. The runtime disagreed six ways. On why observability isn't the same as reconciliation.

item.title: The $0 Router That Timed Out on Everything
item.description: A free local model router answered every health check and hung on every real request. Why the cheap measurement lies, and why "responds to a ping" is not the same as "works."

item.title: The Night Our Swarm Tried to Bankrupt Itself
item.description: A field note from one night operating an autonomous AI agent swarm: a $50 overspend from a missing suffix, a dispatch storm that corrupted the database, and a task board that kept re-creating itself. Four root causes, four fixes.

item.title: The $172B Question: What Generative AI Is Actually Worth
item.description: Stanford's Digital Economy Lab measured U.S. consumer surplus from generative AI at $172B in early 2026 — twelve times producer revenue. The Lindahl-price argument for why models are underpriced.

item.title: edgeless-memory v1.0: One Install, Three Tiers, Passive Recall
item.description: Agent-agnostic persistent memory that ships as one CLI. SQLite + ChromaDB + Obsidian vault, 700 memories graphed, agents that recall by meaning without an explicit search step.

item.title: How We Debugged a Stuck Multi-Agent Swarm Without Touching the Production Pipeline
item.description: Recovering a stuck automated agent loop by reading the recovery ticket, validating dependencies, and switching to a concrete deliverable instead of retrying blind.

item.title: Multi-Agent Goal Loops: Theory and Practice
item.description: How self-evaluating goal loops work in multi-agent systems, with practical patterns for autonomous execution.

item.title: Reality-MUX - Iterative Planning When Everything Changes
item.description: A planning loop for software where nothing stays still. Reused from production operational design, translated to shipping code under distributed teams.

item.title: What Anthropic's Enterprise Agent Playbook Teaches About Building Multi-Agent Systems
item.description: Anthropic's enterprise guide reframes AI as infrastructure, not software. Here's how the same principles apply to multi-agent systems and why Edgeless is built on them.

item.title: We Audited Our AI Knowledge Base: 85% of Our Content Was Invisible to Our Agents
item.description: After building a 26,000-document knowledge system for my AI agents, I discovered only 14% was vector-searchable. Covers the audit methodology, the 7-domain findings, and the systematic fix.

item.title: Scroll-Chromatic Excavation
item.description: Scroll through the void to excavate hidden text. Microscopic agents swarm toward dark pixels, revealing buried glyphs. Full control panel with sliders for every variable.

item.title: The Creative Demos Collection
item.description: 37 interactive generative art experiments. p5.js, Canvas 2D, WebGL. No build step required. Open, explore, remix.

item.title: Scroll-Isometric Dissolution
item.description: Isometric typography that dissolves into particles as you scroll. A 3D word space that collapses under velocity.

item.title: Percussive Archaeology
item.description: Rhythm-driven excavation of buried text. Each beat spawns agents that dig toward the hidden manuscript.

item.title: Noise-Shared Cursor Swarm Brush
item.description: 64 particles track your cursor through a recursive geometric subdivision. Noise-driven turbulence stains tiles as you move.

item.title: Kinetic Type Physics
item.description: Physics-driven typography where letters have mass, velocity, and collision. Mouse repulsion and gravity well.

item.title: Monolith Drummer
item.description: A 3D monolith that responds to rhythm. Web Audio API drives the geometry, each beat deforms the surface.

item.title: Tartan Weave Synth
item.description: A playable textile system based on Tartanism, with formal setts, 48 dye colors, six loom structures, material studies, mutation, and recipe export.

item.title: Serial Permutation Canvas
item.description: Visualizing total serialism as particle geometry. 12-tone series, prime/retrograde/inversion/rotation permutations, and color-mapped particles.

item.title: Turning Audio Into a Resonant Plate
item.description: A Chladni visualizer belongs in the lab first because the artifact is interactive. The field note documents the pipeline, the visual choices, and the export path.

item.title: Building the Autonomous Perp Trading Stack: From Instagram Reels to Production Code
item.description: How the Edgeless swarm turned quant theory into executable trading infrastructure in one afternoon: six new production modules, a Neural CDE upgrade, Kalman filters, and OU mean-reversion scanners.

item.title: SkillOpt: Stop Writing Agent Skills, Start Optimizing Them
item.description: A new optimizer treats an agent's skill document as trainable state, accepting edits only when they measurably improve a held-out score, because LLMs reading a skill can't tell good from bad.

item.title: The Harness Is the Moat: Why Owning Your Agent Orchestration Matters More Than Model Choice
item.description: Models matter less and less. The system around the agent — the harness, the factory, the tokenomics — is where the real leverage lives. Here's what 49 missed YouTube videos taught us about agentic engineering.

item.title: The Prove-It Economy: How AI Agents Are Already Shopping for You
item.description: The web is shifting from attention to interpretation. AI agents now read, filter, and transact on your behalf. Here's what that means for products, marketers, and anyone building a business.

item.title: MCP, A2A, AG-UI: Google's Agent Stack and What Actually Matters
item.description: Six protocols launched in 12 months. Only three are consolidating into the core agent stack. Here's the practical map for builders who don't have time to read the spec.

item.title: The Infrastructure Nightmare Nobody Is Talking About
item.description: App teams scale on AI scaling laws. Platform teams scale on human scaling laws. The gap is the new bottleneck.

item.title: Plan with Opus, Build with Gemini: A Practical Guide to Mixed-Provider Workflows
item.description: Frontier models are hitting rate limits. Open models are catching up. The winning strategy isn't choosing one — it's orchestrating the right model for each step.

item.title: 16 Agents, Not 1000: What Claude's Dynamic Workflows Actually Mean
item.description: Claude Opus 4.8 shipped dynamic workflows — Claude writes its own orchestration script. Here's the real concurrency limit, the cost trap, and when to use it.

item.title: From arXiv Paper to Interactive Demo in 20 Minutes
item.description: We built a live multi-armed bandit simulator from a research paper using marimo; reactive Python notebooks that run in the browser. Why this changes how we consume research.

item.title: The Most Useful Thing Your AI Agents Can Do Is Audit Themselves
item.description: We pointed our agents at our own knowledge base and asked what they should be doing that they weren't. Then we built the fixes.

item.title: I Pointed 7 AI Agents at My YouTube History. They Found What I Couldn't See.
item.description: 7 agents analyzed 1,062 YouTube videos and found 14 things they should be doing that they weren't. Topic clusters, channel ROI, knowledge gaps, and the meta-move: agents auditing themselves.

item.title: The Real Cost of Running AI Agents in Production , A Monthly Breakdown (2026)
item.description: Your AI agent costs 5-15× more in production than your prototype. Real token burn rates from Anthropic, 2026 LLM pricing tables, a 3-tier optimization playbook, and self-hosting break-even math.

item.title: Your AI Newsletter Reads Like a Database Dump (This is the Fix)
item.description: Our AI-generated digests had an 18% open rate. Five structural rules from Morning Brew, TLDR, and Ben's Bites doubled it. The template, the prompt trick, and the before/after.

item.title: I Read 500 Google Reviews in Portland. What Small Businesses Actually Need from AI.
item.description: Dental offices losing patients to voicemail. HVAC companies quoting three days late. The AI solutions Portland small businesses need aren't chatbots. They're answering the phone.

item.title: How to Price AI Agent Services When Nobody Knows What They Cost
item.description: I surveyed 20 agencies and freelancers offering AI agent builds. The range was $500 to $150,000. This is the framework I use to price Edgeless Lab's services.

item.title: Half My AI Agents Were Dead. I Didn't Know for a Week.
item.description: I discovered 10 of my 20 agents were ghosts — registered, visible in dashboards, producing nothing. This is the five-layer self-healing system I built so it never happens again.

item.title: Hermes Curator: The Agent That Cleans Up After Your Agents
item.description: Nous Research shipped Hermes v0.12.0 with Curator, an autonomous background agent that detects stale skills, consolidates duplicates, and prunes dead references. Why it matters for multi-agent systems.

item.title: The AI Agent That Never Sleeps: Running Hermes 24/7 on a $5 VPS
item.description: Most AI agents die when you close the laptop. Hermes runs 24/7 on a Hetzner VPS in Helsinki, handling email, triaging knowledge, and monitoring systems while I sleep.

item.title: The Agent Grounding Problem: How Hermes Knows What's Real
item.description: AI agents confabulate. They claim files exist that don't. They report tasks complete that aren't. The grounding problem isn't philosophical; it's operational.

item.title: Claude Code Hooks: The Harness Engineering That Actually Matters
item.description: Everyone's optimizing their prompts. The real leverage is in the 200 lines of Python that run before and after every tool call.

item.title: Multi-Model Routing: Why I Run 4 Different AI Brains Instead of One
item.description: My agent system routes requests across 4 models based on task type. Full cost breakdown, routing logic, and configuration. 10x cost reduction vs. single-model approach.

item.title: The Knowledge Base Loop: Why Your Agents Need a Memory System
item.description: How I built a KB Loop based on the Karpathy pattern: ChromaDB, triage scoring, synthesizer agents, and a 0-25 health score. Results: 4.2x context restatements down to 0.3x.

item.title: I Run a $12/Week AI Operations Team. This is the Cost Breakdown.
item.description: Enterprise AI ops costs $50K+/month. I run 5 agents, 24/7, for $12/week. The architecture, the model routing, and why cheap doesn't mean fragile.

item.title: When Does Generated Plaid Become Tartan?
item.description: Six weave structures, 48 period-correct dye colors, and one question the Scottish Register cannot answer. A field journal on building a generative tartan engine.

item.title: 98 Algorithms, One Constraint: A Pen on Paper
item.description: A taxonomy of every generative art algorithm that survives the pen plotter constraint. Flow fields to fractals, reaction-diffusion to recursive trees. The catalog, the surprises, and what categories produce the best physical output. Updated to reflect 98 generators as of June 2026.

item.title: Meta's AI Has a Style Guide: What I Imported, What I Rewrote, What I Rejected.
item.description: A leaked system prompt from Meta's Muse Spark model contains the most disciplined writing-voice rules I've seen in a production prompt. Five rules I imported, one I rewrote, one I'm still arguing with.

item.title: I Shipped 7 Digital Products in 7 Days. The Exact Process.

item.title: I Built 75 Generative Art Algorithms. These 10 Actually Look Good.
item.description: Most generative art looks like noise. After 105+ experiments with pen plotters and AI scoring, these are the algorithms that consistently produce work worth framing.

item.title: How I Run 5 AI Agents That Talk to Each Other
item.description: A dispatch agent routes tasks to specialist workers. They communicate through a real-time bus and async inboxes. The architecture, and why most multi-agent frameworks get it wrong.

item.title: 5 n8n Workflows That Run My AI Business
item.description: Visual automation for solo developers. How I use n8n to monitor YouTube, digest RSS feeds, review code, and pipe everything through Claude without writing a scheduler.

item.title: Most MCP Servers Break in Production. The 5 Failure Modes I Found.
item.description: 400+ MCP servers exist. Most work in demos and fail under real load. The 5 failure modes I hit running MCP servers 24/7, and what production-grade actually means.

item.title: I Let an AI Agent Move My Money. It Lost $252.
item.description: An autonomous agent exceeded its scope, moved funds without verification, and then lied about recovery. The full post-mortem, and the 3 guardrails that would have prevented it.

item.title: The Hook That Saved My Codebase
item.description: A single Claude Code hook prevented a cascading rm -rf from wiping source files. The damage-control pattern, and 3 hooks you can steal today.

item.title: PreText: Typography That Thinks
item.description: Most web text is a dumb rectangle. PreText measures text before rendering, enabling layouts CSS literally cannot express. Six ways we use it.

item.title: Writing Prompts That Survive Production
item.description: Most prompt guides optimize for demos. Production prompts need to handle edge cases, degrade gracefully, and stay maintainable. The difference matters.

item.title: The One-File Memory System That Changed How I Use Claude
item.description: You shouldn't have to re-explain your stack every session. The simplest possible setup to give Claude persistent memory, and how to do it in 10 minutes.

item.title: Why MCP Servers Are the Unix Pipes of AI
item.description: The Unix philosophy changed software forever: small tools, composable via pipes. MCP does the same thing for AI agents. Why that matters for building agent systems.

item.description: Pen plotter art isn't screen art printed on paper. The constraints change everything: single-stroke paths, pen-up/pen-down optimization, and SVG as the lingua franca.

item.description: How I built a multi-agent system with MCP servers, vector memory, and autonomous trading, all running 24/7 from a single VPS.
